headline: Prompt Engineer Salary 2026: What US Employers Pay
metaDescription: Prompt engineer salary 2026: median about $126,000, standalone roles $63,000–$180,000, senior $160,000–$216,000. Levels, cities and skills that pay most.

sections.content:
Prompt engineers earn a median of around $126,000 in total pay in the United States in 2026, according to Glassdoor, with standalone roles ranging from roughly $63,000 to $180,000. Indeed puts average base pay near $113,000, while ZipRecruiter reports about $98,000. The spread exists because sources measure different things.

The title covers three different jobs: marketing AI work paying $75,000 to $140,000, applied AI roles paying $135,000 to $275,000, and frontier-lab roles paying $280,000 to $425,000 in base salary. Total compensation at frontier labs can exceed $500,000 with equity.
sections.title: What prompt engineers earn in 2026

sections.content:
Entry-level prompt engineers with strong portfolios earn $85,000 to $120,000 in base pay. Mid-level practitioners earn $120,000 to $160,000, and senior prompt engineers earn $160,000 to $216,000. Lead and principal roles reach $216,000 to $375,000 in base, with total compensation up to $450,000.

There is no dedicated occupation code for prompt engineering, so the Bureau of Labor Statistics tracks the work under software developers, whose median is $135,980. The highest pay attaches to people who are AI engineers with prompt and evaluation depth, not standalone prompt writers.
sections.title: Pay by experience level

sections.content:
Pay is highest in San Francisco, Seattle and New York, where frontier labs and big tech companies cluster. Anthropic's closed Claude Code prompt engineer role listed $300,000 to $405,000 and asked for Python and TypeScript, showing how engineering-level evaluation and coding skills command top pay.

Standalone prompt engineer postings are shrinking as the skill becomes part of broader AI engineering roles. The best-documented postings now ask for evaluation design, retrieval systems and production LLM experience, not just clever prompting.
sections.title: Cities, employers and the job market

sections.content:
The skills that pay most are evaluation design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), LLM fine-tuning and production deployment. Python and TypeScript are the most requested languages, and experience with LangChain, vector databases and agent frameworks adds a clear premium.

A portfolio of shipped AI features beats a certificate. Show before-and-after evaluation results, cost reductions from prompt optimisation, or a production agent you built. Employers pay for measured impact, and the strongest candidates combine prompting with real software engineering.
